> Is there an official recommended workflow or template for packaging a larger model (e.g. Qwen 27B or Gemma 31B), tokenizer, and dependencies so everything can be loaded completely offline during evaluation?

No official way, but plenty of templates you can pick from. You can see a bunch here
https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/arc-prize-2026-arc-agi-3/code?competitionId=133468&sortBy=voteCount&excludeNonAccessedDatasources=true

> If there are additional requirements for minors, could someone point me to the relevant rules?

Yes, minors can participate but must get parental consent, please see form below. Kaggle (not arc) runs this process so they questions will need to be directed towards them.
https://www.kaggle.com/consent-minors-process

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hi everyone! I’m getting started with ARC-AGI-3 and had a couple of questions about the competition.

First, since evaluation has no internet access, I understand that models and dependencies need to be prepared beforehand and attached as Kaggle Datasets. I’ve seen submissions using local Qwen/Gemma models. Is there an official recommended workflow or template for packaging a larger model (e.g. Qwen 27B or Gemma 31B), tokenizer, and dependencies so everything can be loaded completely offline during evaluation? Also, what are the exact GPU and runtime limits available for each submission?

Second, I’m 13 years old. Are participants aged 13–17 allowed to participate in ARC-AGI-3 and be eligible for prizes, assuming any required parent/guardian consent is provided? If there are additional requirements for minors, could someone point me to the relevant rules?

Thanks!
